name: IEC differentiator element (d/dt)
summary: Analogue element marked d/dt whose output is proportional to the rate of change of its input.
description: The differentiator element carries the d/dt function. Its output is proportional to how fast the input changes, so a ramp input gives a constant output and a step input gives a spike. In circuit form it is usually an op-amp with an input capacitor and feedback resistor, often with extra components to limit high-frequency gain.

Rate-of-change functions appear in derivative control terms, df/dt style supervision and edge detection on analogue signals. The drawing should state the time constant and any filtering, because pure differentiation amplifies noise.
The element does not show the noise-limiting network. Reviewers should check that the implementing circuit or software includes one.
readingNotes: Check the time constant and limiting components.
drawingChecklist: Reference the implementing circuit or function block.
distinction: The integrator accumulates the input; the differentiator responds to its rate of change.
